text: Privacy Policy
Effective Date: January 1, 2026 | Last Updated: February 2026
1. Our Commitment to Patient Confidentiality & HIPAA

At Ischys Mental Wellness, preserving your privacy and safeguarding your Protected Health Information (PHI) is fundamental to our care philosophy. We operate in strict compliance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), state health privacy laws in Utah, Texas, and California, and applicable federal confidentiality standards.
2. Information We Collect
We collect personal and clinical information necessary to evaluate, diagnose, and manage psychiatric care safely and effectively:
Personal Identifiers: Name, date of birth, contact information (email, phone, address).
Medical & Psychiatric History: Prior diagnoses, current medications, symptom history, and therapy notes.
Insurance & Billing Details: Payment card details, superbill reimbursement info, and insurance policy data.
Website Usage Data: Anonymized analytical data, browser type, and cookie preferences for website performance optimization.
3. How Your Information is Used
Your health and personal data are used solely for clinical and practice administration purposes, including:
Providing psychiatric evaluations, medication management, and therapeutic consultations.
Scheduling appointments, issuing prescription refills, and maintaining your electronic health record (EHR).
Processing billing transactions and providing superbills for out-of-network insurance reimbursement.
Communicating securely regarding appointment reminders and lab results.
4. Telehealth & Secure Technology

All virtual appointments are conducted via encrypted, HIPAA-compliant video conferencing platforms. We do not record virtual therapy or psychiatric evaluation sessions. Patient communications via our encrypted portal adhere to high-grade security protocols to protect data during transmission.
5. Sharing & Disclosure Restrictions
We will never sell or rent your personal health data to third parties or advertisers. Information is disclosed only under the following limited circumstances:
With Your Explicit Consent: To coordinate care with your therapist, primary care physician, or family members via a signed Release of Information (ROI).
Legal Requirements: As required by law, court order, or mandatory reporting requirements (e.g., imminent harm to self or others, child or elder abuse).
Healthcare Operations: With HIPAA-compliant business associates (e.g., lab facilities, e-prescribing services) bound by strict Business Associate Agreements (BAAs).
6. Your Rights Under HIPAA
As a patient, you hold specific statutory rights regarding your health record:
The right to inspect and request copies of your medical records.
The right to request amendments or corrections to inaccurate records.
The right to request restrictions on how your health information is used or disclosed.
The right to receive an accounting of disclosures of your health data.
